label: paragraph_title
text: THOSE: GUILDS.

label: text
text: If one were dealing with people of balanced mentality it might be said that the logical reasoning of a striker who followed the advice of his Guild and left Hongkong for Canton should be that, once having experienced the folly of putting his trust in Guild officials, he would see to if that in future his monthly contributions should go to some more worthy and personally profitable object. But people who leave situations worth $30-$50 a month—and in some cases considerably more—for the chemical stories of Canton which they

label: text
text: shared with thousands of others, can hardly lay claim to be favoured with that particular class of mentality. It is, doubtful if their faith will be smoker even by a reduction in wages and, in some cases, the entire loss of their employment which has followed the action they were persuaded into taking. The power of the Guilds, then, is not likely to suffer more than a temporary set back and are long the Hongkong Government will be called upon to face again the problem of whether something cannot be done to curb activities which in the present strike have been exercised for evil to the fullest extent.

label: text
text: The present Ordinance allows of interference on the part of the Hongkong Government only when the Guilds are detected in unlawful practices. If the Home Government, with similar powers, cannot place into that category, the action of trade union officials in bringing public services to a standstill, it is doubtful whether the Hongkong Government can act differently in respect of the Chinese Guild officials under their jurisdiction. There appears to be no real reason, however, why the Ordinances should not be amended in order to give the Hongkong Government more control over these pernicious bodies. The trade unionists at Home would kick, of course, and talk glibly about the sacred liberty of the subject—probably it is this more than anything else which has restrained the Government from taking up to the present a step which it certainly is called upon to do in the interests of the foreigner in Hongkong. Were a concensus of opinion possible, it would be found to be in the interests of and in accord with the desire of the greater number of the Guild members themselves. But, after all, why should much notice be taken of a section of the community the ignorance of whom in regard to things Har Eastern the present would maximize least served to throw into minority.

label: text
text: Although the matter was not one of those brothed at Monday night's meeting, if the Government decided to take action, it would undoubtedly have the support of the entire community, for all know that the Guilds are pernicious, and that it is high time that their benevolent activities were effectively curbed.

label: paragraph_title
text: Thế First 100,000.

label: text
text: One of the most popular New York City's "The First Hundred Thousand," which graphically dealt with the first big armies raised for the Front at a time when the irksome conditions of war time were novel as well as incommoding. It requires no great strain of the imagination to draw on analogy between that "First Hundred Thousand" and the first hundred thousand meals served during the local strike by the Hongkong Hotels, Limited. The conditions since June 19 have been akin to a state of war in more respects than one; they have to many been irksome, but they have also been novel and likewise incommoding. Looking to the unique circumstances under which the hotels, in common with businesses and households, were left without sufficient labour to "carry on," it must generously be conceded that the supplying of an average of 2,500 meals a day establishes a record of which the whole community must be proud. Whilst the forces behind the strike movement sought—and are seeking—to create an economic blockade of the Colony, they have been dealt a vital blow in regard to the morale of the strikers by witnessing the Hongkong Hotels not only "making good," but even exceeding pre-strike records to the extent of serving a hundred thousand meals, thus incidentally enabling hundreds of residents and visitors to eat as well as to work. The position of the usual state of war has been reversed. An army can only march on its stomach, as some great General once observed in effect. In the case of Hongkong the army of strikers has little or nothing to march on, whilst the peaceful residents have had not the slightest need to worry about the needs of "the interior," so well have those been catered for by Mr. Taggart and his battalion of volunteer workers. Many compliments have already been showered on the Hotels since the strike began, but they have signalised the best compliment to their own services in the feat of serving a hundred thousand meals.

label: text
text: A "HAT TRICK": 17 WICKETS.

label: text
text: Very little can prevent Yorkshire from winning the county cricket championship for the fourth year in succession. At this stage of the season they hold a commanding lead over Surrey their nearest rivals, even though they have dropped two points in each of three recent matches. Of their remaining fixtures the champions have to play Lancashire at Sheffield, Warwick and Sussex at home, and the following away: —Leicester. Essex, Hants. Sussex and Surrey (at the Oval). The only matches to cause them unrest may be the tussle with the Red Rose and the visit to the Oval. Even if Yorkshire lost both these encounters the probability is that they would finish up on top.

label: text
text: Surrey's percentage does not change as will be seen from the results detailed below and the championship table to date. It is interesting to note, as pointed out in the "China Mail" about a week or so ago, that Reuter has cabled the fact of Surrey's crowd eagerly waiting for their idol to make a century and thus tie the record of Dr. Grace.

label: text
text:
"Tipped" by "Plum" Warner as likely champions, Lancashire has disappointed and are now third. They and Surrey are the only ones left in the running as Middlesex is virtually out of the race.
If interest is to be sustained to the last, it will be necessary for some of the so-called weaker counties to spring a surprise on Yorkshire.

label: text
text: In the results it will also be seen that V. W. C. Jupp, the former Sussex amateur and now the Norphans secretary, has performed the "hat trick" and Parker, the Gloucester professional has brought off another astonishing bowling feat. Herbert Sutcliffe, the Yorkshire opening batman who won the admiration of the Australians by his batting in the last series of Test Matches, has struck form again.
